verdict.headline: Oil jumps and the bond selloff resumes after Trump rejects Iran's Hormuz plan
verdict.label: Pre-market: Brent ~$108.48 (+4%), WTI ~$96.16 (+4%); S&P 500 futures -0.5%, Nasdaq-100 futures -0.8%; 2Y 4.916% (+5 bp), 10Y 5.219%, 30Y 5.529%; gold ~-3% below $4,200; DXY 101.15; BTC ~$83,100.
verdict.rationale_short: Trump's rejection of Iran's seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz put Brent up about 4% near $108.50, above Thursday's $106.60 settle, so the market has taken out the rest of Friday's deal premium. Unlike last week, when the thirty-year rose on inflation expectations while oil fell, oil and yields are now pushing the same way: the two-year is up 5 basis points to 4.916%, the ten-year is back at last week's 5.22% high and the thirty-year trades near 5.53%. Gold's 3% fall and a two-month high in the dollar say the market is pricing higher oil through the Fed rather than as a reason to buy havens. One signal cuts the other way: October hike odds are quoted near 70-72%, below Friday's 76%. A Brent settle back under $106.60 with the thirty-year under 5.44% would say the morning moves were a reaction to headlines rather than a repricing.
verdict.lede_short: Oil rose about 4% to near $108.50 after Trump rejected Iran's plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and stock futures fell 0.5%. Unlike last week, oil and bond yields are rising together: the two-year leads, the thirty-year trades near 5.53%, and gold's 3% drop says the market is pricing this through the Fed, not as a flight to safety. A Brent settle back under $106.60 with the thirty-year under 5.44% would undo that read.

supporting_data.label: Brent rose about 4% to $108.48 and WTI about 4% to $96.16 after Trump rejected Iran's Hormuz conditions — Brent is back above Thursday's $106.60 settle, so Friday's deal premium is gone.

The two-year rose more than 5 basis points to 4.916%, the ten-year to 5.219% and the thirty-year traded at 5.529% — the front end leading ties the selloff to the Fed path, and the ten-year is back at last week's 5.22% high.
Spot gold fell about 3% below $4,200 to its lowest since August 5 — gold falling on an escalation day says higher oil is being priced through rates, not as a reason to buy havens.
Dow futures fell 251 points, S&P 500 futures 0.5% and Nasdaq-100 futures 0.8% — a larger drop than Sunday night's 0.2%, led by the growth stocks most exposed to yields.

Nvidia added $150 billion to its buyback for a $235 billion total and is up about 1.5% pre-market while the semiconductor ETF falls about 2% — the largest chipmaker is holding up as the rest of the sector sells off on yields.

The Kospi fell 2.7% as it reopened after Chuseok, with Samsung Electronics down 5.43% and SK Hynix down 5.05% — Asia's memory makers took the yield and Oracle data-center news in one session, days before Micron reports.

watchlist_mentions.note: Up about 1.5% pre-market after adding $150 billion to its buyback, for a $235 billion total, and launching AI-agent containment software, while the semiconductor ETF falls about 2%.
Down about 3% pre-market after a gain of almost 13% last week on the Muse agent launch, with no new company news.
Reports fiscal Q4 on September 30. Samsung and SK Hynix fell more than 5% each in Seoul on Monday, so the print arrives against weaker memory-stock sentiment.
Up about 1.5% pre-market with Brent up 4%, less than half of oil's move.

trade_setups.thesis: The thirty-year trades near 5.53% against Friday's 5.488% close, with oil now adding to the inflation-expectations pressure that drove last week's rise. A close above 5.44% would be the third straight above the 2007 peak.
trade_setups.entry: Thirty-year 5.529% against 5.5% and 5.44%; ten-year 5.219% against last week's 5.22% high.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close under 5.44% would say the oil move is not reaching the long end.
trade_setups.horizon: Today's close through the September 30 PCE

trade_setups.thesis: Brent is up about 4% near $108.50 after the rejection, above Thursday's $106.60 settle, as Iran holds its terms and Qatari mediators are reported to meet both sides.
trade_setups.invalidation: A settle back under $106.60, or a formal US counter-offer, would put Friday's $104.32 back in range.

trade_setups.thesis: The semiconductor ETF is down about 2% pre-market and the Kospi's memory makers fell more than 5%, while Nvidia rises on its buyback. Rates, not company news, are driving most of the sector's move.
trade_setups.entry: SOXX about -2% pre-market; Samsung -5.43%, SK Hynix -5.05% in Seoul.
trade_setups.invalidation: Micron's fiscal Q4 on September 30 and AMD's October 1 price increase test whether higher rates are hitting AI demand or only valuations.
